chunks: The obligatory prayer of travel is two units (rak'at), except for Maghrib, for surely the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) left it upon its state in travel and residence.
One does not pray anything of the voluntary prayers of the day in travel, and one does not leave off anything of the voluntary prayers of the night.

Night Prayer (salat al-layl) is not permissible from the beginning of the night except in travel. When the person performs its make-up prayer (qada), it is better for him than praying it at the beginning of the night.

key_terms.ركعتان: Two units of prayer (rak'at) — the shortened format
key_terms.فرض السفر: The obligatory shortened prayer of travel (qasr)
key_terms.قضى: Make-up prayer (qada) — performing a prayer at a time other than its prescribed time
key_terms.نوافل الليل: Voluntary nighttime prayers, including salat al-layl

ai.seo_question: How many rak'at are prayed in travel according to Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines the rules for shortening (qasr) prayer during travel. The obligatory prayers are reduced to two rak'at, with Maghrib as the sole exception since the Prophet (SAWW) maintained it at three in both travel and residence. Additionally, daytime voluntary prayers (nawafil) are suspended in travel, while nighttime voluntary prayers remain obligatory. A special dispensation is given for Night Prayer: while it is normally only prayed in the latter portion of the night, travelers may pray it at the beginning of the night, and performing the make-up (qada) is even more virtuous.
